record.original_question: For parking problems on random trees, especially in regimes involving heavy-tailed car-arrival distributions and frozen modifications of the Erdos-Renyi process, can one prove scaling-limit results in Gromov-weak or Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov type metric topologies, and do the resulting limits relate to additive and multiplicative coalescents or to inhomogeneous continuum random trees?

evidence.quote: At present, issues of studying parking problems in different metric topologies remains largely unaddressed. Contat and Curien (2023) have themselves pointed to appropriate contributions to follow in this sense ... It seems as expected that scaling limit results, in particular when combined with frozen modification of the Erdos-Renyi process would combine additive and multiplicative coalescent, due to the connection with Gromov-weak and Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov topologies. Limiting results could relate to inhomogenous continuum random trees as described in Bhamidi, van der Hofstad and Sen (2018).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the parking process on a random tree, defined as follows. Let $T_n$ be a random rooted tree on $n$ vertices (for example, a uniform Cayley tree, a critical Galton–Watson tree with a prescribed offspring law, or more generally a random tree with a given degree sequence). At each vertex $v\in T_n$, an independent number $A_v$ of cars arrives, where the $A_v$ are i.i.d. with common law $\mu$ on $\{0,1,2,\dots\}$. Cars are then processed sequentially: each car tries to park at its arrival vertex; if that vertex is already occupied, the car drives along the unique path toward the root until it finds the first empty vertex and parks there, or exits the tree from the root if no empty vertex is found. Write $\mathcal{C}_1(n)\ge\mathcal{C}_2(n)\ge\dots$ for the connected components of parked cars, equipped with the induced graph metric and the counting measure on parked cars.

Consider in addition the frozen Erdős–Rényi process, a variant of the Erdős–Rényi random graph process in which connected components carrying cycles are "frozen" and no longer participate in further mergers, coupled to the parking process in the critical window.

Address the following:

(a) When the car-arrival distribution $\mu$ has a heavy tail (say $\mu(\{k\})\sim c\, k^{-\alpha-1}$ for some $\alpha\in(1,2)$), and at criticality for the parking phase transition, do the components $(\mathcal{C}_i(n))_{i\ge 1}$, suitably rescaled, converge in the Gromov-weak topology and in the Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topology to a sequence of random compact measured metric spaces?

(b) If such scaling limits exist, can they be described in terms of (the entrance boundary of) the additive coalescent, the multiplicative coalescent, or a hybrid coalescent obtained from the frozen modification of the Erdős–Rényi process; and are the limiting metric spaces realized as inhomogeneous continuum random trees of the kind constructed in connection with the additive coalescent and critical inhomogeneous random graphs?

Prove or disprove the existence of these scaling limits and identify the limiting objects.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Contat–Curien and Contat–Laulin (2023–2025) has established scaling limits for parking on critical Galley/Galton–Watson trees toward the Brownian growth-fragmentation tree and analyzed parking on the random recursive tree, but a general scaling-limit theory in Gromov-weak / Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov topologies for heavy-tailed car-arrival laws together with the frozen Erdős–Rényi coupling, with limits identified in terms of additive/multiplicative coalescents and inhomogeneous continuum random trees, has not been established and is explicitly listed as an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Short survey of results and open problems for parking problems on random trees
status_evidence.snippet: At present, issues of studying parking problems in different metric topologies remains largely unaddressed.
status_evidence.claim: The metric-topology scaling-limit question for parking on random trees is identified as largely open.

status_evidence.title: Parking on Cayley trees & Frozen Erdös-Rényi
status_evidence.snippet: phase transition for the size of the components of parked cars using a modification of the multiplicative coalescent called the frozen multiplicative coalescent
status_evidence.claim: Frozen multiplicative coalescent governs the size phase transition; metric-level scaling limits are a natural next step.

status_evidence.title: The multiplicative coalescent, inhomogeneous continuum random trees, and new universality classes for critical random graphs
status_evidence.snippet: ICRT scaling limits for critical inhomogeneous random graphs
status_evidence.claim: ICRTs are the candidate limits suggested by the analogy with critical random graphs.

status_evidence.title: Parking on trees with a (random) given degree sequence
status_evidence.snippet: parking on trees with given degree sequence
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress exists for parking on random trees with prescribed degrees, but not the full Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov limit in the heavy-tailed/frozen regime.
